CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Semarang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance duties with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
4. Regional House of Representatives of Semarang Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.

7. Human Rights are a set of rights inherent in the nature and existence of human beings as creatures of God Almighty and constitute His gift that must be respected, upheld and protected by the state, law, Government, and every person for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
10. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, irrespective of their marital status, on a basis of equality between men and women.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
13. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children.
15. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
16. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.

Female victims of disaster are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals and between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women that causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.

Women have equal rights with men, however in certain discriminatory conditions, the government is obliged to implement affirmative action so that the rights of women and women in vulnerable groups need to receive protection so that they do not experience violence and can live decent lives according to the principles of humanity, equality and justice.

Women's empowerment and women's protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To carry out these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data.

The Government of Semarang Regency as the party that has the authority to regulate and protect the citizens of Semarang Regency, deems it necessary to continuously carry out and formulate regulations in order to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and women's protection in Semarang Regency.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

What is meant by victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act.
Witnesses and victims will receive legal protection.

The retrieved passages match the Indonesian text and the judge correctly noted the lack of an explicit physical-violence type. Thus the golden 'Yes' appears incorrect under a strict 'explicit mention' criterion.

(1) Protection of women includes:
a. social protection;
b. economic protection;
c. legal protection.
(2) Social protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is to ensure the survival of women in the form of social protection in order to ensure the fulfillment of decent living needs.
(3) Economic protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is to prevent and address the risk of vulnerability resulting from shocks and social vulnerability of a person, family, group and/or community for the survival of women.
(4) Legal protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented in terms of providing protection to women who become witnesses and victims of acts of violence and discrimination.

Article 21

a. access to proper housing;
b. health services;
c. information access services and legal consultation; and
d. post-disaster recovery.

Article 1

2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance duties with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.

8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SEMARANG REGENCY
NUMBER 1 OF 2015
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or seized by anyone. In the context of Upholding Human Rights (HAM) to guarantee justice for every individual, efforts are made to prevent all forms of unbalanced treatment or treatment deemed detrimental to other parties, whether between individuals, between groups of individuals, or between individuals and between government and society, including the process of marginalization of women that causes women to be vulnerable to acts of violence, discrimination and exploitation in both domestic and public spheres.

Women have equal rights with men, however in certain discriminatory conditions, the government is obliged to implement affirmative action so that the rights of women and women in vulnerable groups need to receive protection so that they do not experience violence and can live decent lives according to the principles of humanity, equality and justice.

Women's empowerment and women's protection are implemented in order to realize gender equality and justice. To carry out these affairs, efforts are needed to increase the capacity of women's resources and strengthen gender mainstreaming institutions, through gender mainstreaming strategies and gender-disaggregated data.

The Government of Semarang Regency as the party that has the authority to regulate and protect the citizens of Semarang Regency, deems it necessary to continuously carry out and formulate regulations in order to provide guarantees for women's empowerment and women's protection in Semarang Regency.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

Article 21
Female victims of disaster are women who suffer or die as a result of natural and social disasters.
Post-disaster recovery includes psychological services for victims, health services, residential facilities, facilitation of public facilities and infrastructure and restoration of economic access as well as population data services and legal aid.

Article 23
(1) The Implementation of Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 13 letter j is in the context of providing legal protection and/or health recovery.
(2) Protection for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal assistance;
b. assistance following the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. rehabilitation and social reintegration; and
d. health services.

It mentions trafficking only as a prevention element within protection for female commercial sex workers (Pasal 22(2)(c) "mencegah terjadinya perdagangan orang"; Penjelasan Pasal 24(2) mentions prevention/handling of trafficking against women and children in the context of P2TP2A services). There is no explicit provision of protection measures targeted specifically to trafficking victims. The judge’s 'No' matches the Indonesian text and retrieved passages; the golden 'Yes' likely over-credits trafficking-prevention language as victim-protection coverage.

a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of program and activity planning with related SKPD; and
c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
(2) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning is further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
(3) The formulation of policy for program and activity planning for the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is coordinated by the SKPD responsible for regional development planning.
(4) The budgeting of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter b is implemented through general budget policy as set forth in the APBD.
(5) The implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 25 letter c is implemented through:
a. implementation of programs and activities as set forth in the SKPD budget document; and
b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of programs and activities with related SKPD.
(6) The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in Article 25 letter d is implemented through:
a. conducting monitoring and evaluation periodically on the implementation of programs and activities that have been implemented; and
b. making reports periodically.
